criteria: Continue if, on every dataset, the best discovery arm loses <= 5 points per held-out genome against grouped all-read assembly with >= 50% fewer assembly-input pairs and lower end-to-end wall time and peak RAM; revise if failures are confined to identifiable cases with a plausible fix; stop if losses are broad or end-to-end cost is not lower.

hard.description: Hard benchmark: 12 samples x 500k pairs, 3 communities, congeners, thin, rare, and common novel genomes

pilot.description: M1 pilot: 8 samples x 1M pairs, 2 communities, species-holdout catalogue

split.description: Pilot plus a novel genome at ~1x in all 8 samples (M6 split-genome scenario)

design: Factorial per dataset: input {all reads, discovery pools} x grouping {per sample, metadata communities, all samples pooled}, plus pooled iteration (residual-only, recruitment; 3 rounds) on the grouped discovery coassembly. Every command at 16 threads / 64 GiB, serially, under /usr/bin/time. Discovery arms' end-to-end cost includes profiling, catalogue indexing, and mapping.
evaluation_notes: communities: per-community MetaQUAST (each arm's contigs from groups containing that community's samples; gate per held-out genome). Iterate arms are shared sets, evaluated whole with every community (evaluator default since M7, owner decision): every pool maps to one set, and round-1 acceptance drops contigs contained in another group's contig; iterate-round1 is the accepted union of the grouped coassemblies. origin_attributed_iterate_evaluation: iterate contigs attributed to the group that assembled them (--origin-arm, the M6 lens), kept to document that artifact. correctness_all_genomes: every contig of an arm against all source genomes of the dataset, so contigs of a genome confined to one community are not scored against another community's congeners. Peak RSS for the cost check is /usr/bin/time's maximum resident set size (largest single process); concurrent_mapping_rss_bound_kib sums the four largest mapping stages (discover ran with --jobs 4).
